utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor vs. Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber was informed that you would like to address the Chamber. Please do so. Let's all try to keep in mind that, if possible, we'd like to finish with both witnesses still in the Hague in this moment now. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I will be briefer than usual. Thank you. I want to say that the Defence is going to suggest that the Prosecution concentrate on giving us a translation of this famous document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that General Galic is not receiving any translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there -- is it is matter of the channel chosen? It should be on six. [Interpretation] Is it working now? [In English] Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. What we suggest is that the Prosecution should give us again, if it intends to submit this document which we don't and can't accept in any case, we suggest that they give us a translation which could be more or less correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is the same. Could someone assist General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The General has just told me that it is correct now. If it is not working, the general will tell me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We compared the two texts until late in the evening yesterday and there is certain discrepancies and I would like to thank the Trial Chamber for the attention it has paid to this. There are certain discrepancies which are such that we don't see how this text in its translated form, because we have translation from English to Serbian and Serbian to English, so we don't think that in the translated states it should not be submitted as such. It is not a document that one can rely on. I have made a list of 20 pages listing the errors. At times, there are places which are completely invented which can't be found in the audio cassette, and which are found in the English, that is to say, the translated version. This problem occurs on several occasions. Once again this is not acceptable. So very briefly, if the Prosecution could provide us with this, if they could make this effort to give us a text which would be more or less well translated and on the basis of which we could work, that would be good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to keep in mind that the B/C/S text is not a translation of the English or the English a translation of the B/C/S. It is the words spoken as such, but, as I understand, and the Chamber did not check it on the basis of the tapes that there might be mistakes or errors in the transcript as such as well. If finally we would have to use these texts, if there are any errors in translation made at that time, that does not take away that at least then now the words spoken at that time which can be checked on the tape by the witness should be properly translated. I will first ask -- so we will pay proper attention to that before giving a final decision on whether or not this document can be admitted. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that there is nevertheless -- there are nevertheless elements which independently of the translation or the lack of translation are not understandable to the extent that there are things which are contained in one text, but aren't in the other. So yet again as I said the other day, there is a lot of the confusion there and one can't make anything out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fortunately the witness is here, so if there is any problem we could ask him to -- and we asked him already yesterday to see whether there would be any parts which were in need of either correction or completion. But before doing so, I would like to -- we will pay attention to that when the witness is in the courtroom again. I have a few other issues on which the Chamber would like to draw your attention as well. Let me just find them. I have a few questions for the parties before we continue. First of all, about the maps, the Chamber, as it stands now, on the basis of the information received until now has difficulties in accepting the maps according to the new software, especially it's not clear in what -- to what extent the basis of the maps could be that precise as to make a distinction between 2 metres, 3 metres, 4 metres, which, of course, for the lines of sight might be of importance. It might be not too difficult to understand how difference in elevation of 30, 40 or 50 metres could be easily detected, but what would be the difference between a van standing somewhere and making the elevation two metres higher. How has this been measured? And that could be of importance for the very specific lines of sight as we find them on the new map. So the Chamber would need more information before giving a final decision in admitting this new software technology. Next issue is the 92 bis statements. As far as the recollection of the Chamber goes on the 29th of September it was announced that the 92 bis statements could be expected somewhere in the next month. Could the Defence inform the Chamber on whether any request has been made to the Registrar, whether the statements have been prepared or not? I see Ms. Pilipovic that you are nodding no. Does that mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not yet, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that not even a request has been made to the Registrar in order to start with the proceedings necessary to come to an acceptable 92 bis statement to be introduced at trial?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that hasn't been done yet. I think that we will be doing that over the next few days recollect but I don't think that there will be many 92 bis statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, we will see. But please pay proper attention to that issue and do it as quickly as possible, because otherwise we might get stuck somewhere in the near future. Next question would be: When will the expert reports --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the expert Jovanovic be filed?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with regard to the expert report of Mr. Jovanovic, I think that Mr. Jovanovic won't be an expert who will be presenting the problems of his analysis, but at the end of this day and when we leave for Belgrade, we will think about who the expert will be and very soon inform you who the expert will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would this mean -- still a start would be made in drafting an expert report.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The expert report is being worked on, but I would like to -- it is in progress, but I would like to inform the Chamber that it won't be Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the next issue in respect of expert reports, first of all, in general, I think the Chamber has made clear what it considers to be an expert. An expert is a person whom by virtue of some specialised knowledge, skill, or training can assist the trier of fact to understand or determine an issue in dispute, that is how the Chamber defined what the expert is in the decision concerning the expert witnesses, Ewa Tabeau and Richard Philipps. And at several occasions, both on the 2nd of August and also when discussing the expert report of Mr. Higgs, the Chamber has given some additional guidance to the parties. That is the four elements then mentioned of what the Chamber expects from an expert. The first one, that there should be full transparency of the established and the assumed facts on which the expert relies. Second element is that the methods used when applying his or her knowledge, experience or skills to form the opinion of the expert should be also transparent. It is -- some of the determinations to be made are the exclusive domain of the Chamber and not of the expert. So therefore I invite the parties to - at least at this moment the Defence - to reread all these requirements very carefully and see whether your expert reports are meeting these standards. And if not, perhaps that either additional information will be given or -- because the Chamber, for example, has not found for every witness a full and -- curriculum, a curriculum which would explain why this person is supposed to be having special skills or knowledge. Sometimes it is also unclear, at least it seems unclear, what is the factual basis on which the expert has based his or her expert opinion. For example, sometimes it seems that the expert is relying on statements of witnesses, so not testimony but statements of witnesses, that might be even be unknown to the Chamber, whereas it also seems that sometimes the expert might have no knowledge of the testimony given in this court on specific incidents. So, therefore, it is very important for the Chamber to know exactly what has been the factual basis on which the -- the factual sources on which the expert relied. Sometimes it seems that experts base their report on the existence of certain facts without an explanation as to the basis on which the witness assumed these facts to be true. If I just may give you an example, for example, the Chamber has read in one of the reports that the Markale market incident resulted in eight people killed. It is not clear to the Chamber on what basis the witness has assumed or established this fact, that is unclear. And at the same time, one could wonder whether it is not in the exclusive domain of the Chamber to establish whether and if how many people were killed and/or injured on this shelling incident. The Chamber would like to make quite clear to the Defence that even if an expert appears in this court and testifies, that the Chamber will always keep in its mind the requirements necessary to accept parts or the whole of a report as an expert report, and the mere fact that part of a statement will be admitted into evidence or -- of a report will be admitted in evidence or even if the report is such will be admitted in evidence. That does not mean that the Chamber will accept all the findings of that expert. It should be totally clear that in order to accept findings of an expert that the factual basis, that the methodology and that the transparency both to the factual sources and to the methodology used, should be met. Finally, but this is in respect of a specific report, if the Chamber is not mistaken, the report of the expert Terzic was not announced previously, and the Chamber takes the position that one would wonder whether this report would have sufficient relevance to be admitted, and therefore invites the party to make submissions as to the relevance of specifically this report. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you remind me of the name that doesn't appear clearly, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: T-E-R-Z-I-C, if I am making no mistake. Yes. It is the report on the past of Bosnia-Herzegovina written by Dr. Slavinko Terzic. Then I would like to turn for one second into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. I think now we are come at a moment where we could ask witness DP30 to re-appear. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we do that, could I raise some matters very quickly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly in relation to the issue of the interview of this witness, it would still be helpful to me to know with some confidence whether ultimately in one form or another the -- a record of that interview will be accepted into evidence. Could I respectfully suggest that the safest course at this stage from that perspective would be for the Prosecution to tender copies of the tapes themselves, and in due course to provide, that is to tender, formal transcripts -- I am sorry -- formal translations of the B/C/S transcript into evidence. Mr. President, since this problem has come to light yesterday, Prosecution has taken steps to obtain from CLSS formal translations of B/C/S transcripts of interviews where they were done of Defence witnesses. That may mean that unless those translations are available beforehand, that we will not have them at the time that some of the Defence witnesses are called. With that in mind, I proposed today to remind the Defence of which witnesses on their list have been interviewed and to seek their cooperation by not calling those witnesses until we have provided them with copies of the formal translations. I emphasise that we are seeking the highest priority for that task from CLSS. So, Mr. President, the first issue is whether the Trial Chamber can, at this stage, indicate that it will accept into evidence at least a copy of the actual audio tape. With that knowledge, I intend to be very brief with the witness. Secondly, we were informed by the Defence a few days ago that -- of the identity of four witnesses that the Defence proposes to call in the first week in January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are referring to the Ukrainian witnesses, or if I may call them --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Two Ukrainian and two Russian. We will not be ready to cross-examine those witnesses unless the Defence provides us immediately with the rank of those individuals and their dates of birth. I did raise this last week in court and I understood that we would have received that information yesterday. We still haven't received it. I am concerned that this is the last opportunity that the Prosecution has to raise the matter in the presence of the Trial Chamber, if we don't receive it today. On that issue, might I simply remind the Trial Chamber that of course we will need the presence of the interpreters in the Russian and Ukrainian language in that first week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me first start, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One more matter, Mr. President. You may recall that - I think - some weeks ago now we raised the issue that we did not have -- we were not provided with translations of the appendixes to the reports of Professor Cavoski and also Dr. Kosova [phoen]. We did raise that in a meeting with the Defence shortly after I raised it in the Trial Chamber, and we were told that we would receive some more information. We have not received any information. And we do still take the position that we require those appendixes to be in a language of the Tribunal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very briefly because we are running out of time. But as far as the transcript is concerned, our position is very clear. In addition, and you have noticed this yourself, the witness made quite a few corrections with his own hand, and instead of saving time, we have unfortunately wasted a lot more time. In addition this is a document that hasn't been signed by the witness, that hasn't been provided to him at the time and perhaps isn't accepted by him. So we can't accept that one tenders a transcript which is sometimes incorrect, as a matter of principle we can't accept it, and in a situation which we don't know what the was like, and it wasn't signed by the person concerned, and it was never officially accepted by this person. And I think that certain information, the ranks, were provided to the Prosecution and the dates of birth as well. And Ms. Pilipovic could add a few more details with regard to this information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as the dates of birth are concerned of the four witnesses that we proposed in our submission of the 6th of December and we gave the information regarding their ranks and the time that they spent in Sarajevo during the relevant period, and we also gave the information who was there at which time. I have two -- for two witnesses, copies of their passports. I have already submitted them to the victims and witness unit. And then I will then submit the information to my learned colleagues about their dates of birth and expect that during the course of today I will get the information for the other two witnesses. I, of course, regard this as my duty, as my obligation, and I will do this while I am still in The Hague. I will provide the relevant information. And I have informed my learned colleague last week that I will make sure that I do everything by the end of today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think there were four issues. The first one, I will deal with it later, that is the indication on whether the statement or at least the audio tape could be admitted into evidence. The four witnesses, rank and date of birth, I do understand that it's either provided or on its way. So perhaps during the break you could check when exactly the full information will be provided. Then we have the translations prepared by the Prosecution of statements given by Defence witnesses. I take it that the parties will, at least the Defence will, consult the Prosecution in order to, if necessary, reschedule or at least organise the appearance of these witnesses in such a way that no -- not unnecessary problems will arise from the nonavailability of the translations of their statements. And then finally, I did not hear an answer yet on the translation of the appendixes to the Kosova [phoen] report. I take it that the Prosecution will be informed during the next break about the point of view of the Defence. Then let's return to the first issue you mentioned. Let me just confer. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, to give you an indication about whether an audio version or a written version would be admitted to the Chamber, the Chamber would prefer first to ask a few questions to the witness of the homework he did yesterday, and to find out whether the written version or the audio version would be a sufficiently clear basis to proceed upon. Madam Usher, could you please escort Witness DP30 into courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. DP30, may I first of all remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony? Yes. Mr. DP30, I was informed that you worked until late yesterday and that you -- we received copies of the, I would say, the redacted version, and I saw that you not only paid attention to the -- to the Bosnian Serbian Croatian version, but also a bit to the English version. May I first ask you in general terms, apart from any specific points to be corrected or to be adjusted or to be given a further explanation, that in general, does the text as you found it on paper reflect the main lines of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that the text has been rather inexpertly translated. I have a feeling that all of this has first been translated into English and then after that it was translated into B/C/S. So in many sentences some words are repeated. Sentences do not have meaning. And even some questions I have a feeling have been changed, and as such are not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We can check on the basis of the audio tape, and if necessary, we could just make you hear a small portion of that in order to see whether this is your voice giving a statement. We could check that. May I ask you to quickly go with me and could perhaps the witness be provided with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I first ask you where you have written a "T" could perhaps the witness be provided -- it should not be put on the ELMO since it will be a document under seal. But where you have written a "T," could you explain what you meant with a "T"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was thinking of translation. I meant in relation to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we perhaps quickly go through your remarks in the Bosnian Serbian Croatian version of this document. I would very much like to concentrate in order to see if we can conclude your testimony today, to concentrate on those parts that need further explanation or where you that the way we find it in the text might create confusion. So rather not on every single detail of a word which would not create confusion, but is not perfectly translated. So I find on page 2 that you added a few words, approximately one-third from above. Could you explain. It reads "approximately like Koliko" or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, I believe that it so. And here it says "indistinct or inaudible."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you filled in the words that you, as far as your recollection go, have spoken at that time and where the audio could not be deciphered. Yes. Could you please slowly repeat the words so that they are translated to us, the words you have written. It is already "approximately like Koliko" yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, these are the words that should be here, and I believe that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, then we turn to page 3 where you, on the second line, you filled in something as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 3 I put in what my post was, which is the commander of the 2nd technical warehouse. And what cannot be heard is "of ammunition and explosive and mining devices."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then approximately in the middle you have stricken out a few words and replaced it by another word. Could you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here several words were added in translation, and they do not correspond to the text. What I thought it was is that "according to the plan of the superior command, mobilisation was carried out according to the wartime establishment. And that the warehouse should have had about 350 people and that the department or the section in Renovica, some 30 kilometres away should have 150 people."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we find better in the English text. As far as I can see what you are saying now is more in accordance with the English text. Okay then you added something in the left margin approximately in the middle of the page. Could you explain what that -- if you just read what you have written.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A question and answer are missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and are you telling us that they are in the English text or have you not checked that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in the English text, is there, and while in this one it is not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So there is a divergence between the B/C/S version and the English version. Then I see that you corrected a little bit later on the word "general" I think I saw such a word in the English text. Then could you please turn the page 4. Do I have to understand just below the middle of the page that a word should be in a different place; is that how I have to understand that line with a -- what seems to be a small arrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the text there are a lot of additions like that, these superfluous words that are being repeated and they even make a sentence meaningless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you have pointed at these parts of the text, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mostly either underlined them or crossed them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then just below the middle of the page I see a bit longer line starting with the word - I certainly will pronounce it not correctly - "povecani" what does that mean, that line that you have drawn there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 5?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 4. It is just below the words "sto je vojska imala odredeni." You see there is a line from "povecani" to...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. As far as I remember nothing in particular was undertaken towards civilians except that the army had a certain increased level of readiness, which means that in the sentence words are not in their proper order. So the sentence has no meaning. Further on the translation itself is interrupted, so as a whole the text could correspond to the translation but it isn't correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then further down on this page you added one word in the right margin and three words in the left margin. Could you please read them so that we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is about the soldiers of Muslim nationality who in spite of Alija Izetbegovic's call not to respond to the military service, still remained serving their military service, that is, they did not wish to leave the army service until they completed it. Because of this situation, the Croats themselves didn't respond either. So what I have explained is because of such a situation, the Croats themselves no longer responded to the JNA except for some individuals, for mostly individuals. So that is how it should be. And I believe that that is what I said yesterday during my testimony, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let's now turn to the page 5. Page 5, as far as I could decipher, the following order of questions and answers at the beginning is a bit divergent from what we find in the English text. Could you please read what you have written to the left -- in the left margin on page 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wrote a question and answer are interrupted. And in the English version it is all at once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we have to check that on the basis of the original audio tapes. Then in the middle of the page you did add one word just above where it reads "Brodove."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "They were taken to the Ploce harbour in order to be boarded on to ships."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is about the ammunition as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see, I take it, some smaller correction on that page. Could we please turn to page 6. You have written something after the first answer written on that page. It seems that you wanted to insert something. Could you read what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is inserted here and some answer in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the English version correct in this respect, as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember now. This is -- was, as far as I remember, about the warehouse, the Faletici warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we have to pay proper attention to your exact words on the original tape. Then a bit lower down it seems that you added something as to the structure of the JNA. Is that an addition or is that a correction? You will find it in the right margin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Again the translation is the problem. Some words are repeated, unnecessarily repeated, I don't think that is how they are in the English version. And mostly the answer is that 744th logistics base -- yes. In fact, it is the question. "Where was the location of the 744th logistics base within the structure of the JNA?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's how you understood the question to be. Then a little bit further down you added one word just above where it reads "twenty." Would you please read that word you added.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When the JNA left after the 20th of May, the logistics base gave a new -- received a new name, the new demarcation as the 27th logistics base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. That's more or less in conformity with the English text. Then could we turn to page 7. You added in the fourth paragraph, you added a few words. Could you please read your answer as in your recollection it should have been.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, when we took the ammunition from Pretis that was produced there, as I said, throughout the war in the immediate vicinity of Muslim positions, for the ammunition taken I had to send reports every day to my superior command, that is, to the command of the 27th logistics base, just like other warehouses from the base, and the base then forwarded them to the Main Staff. That's what the answer should be like, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you added a few words a bit further down near to where the numbers "92" and "93" appears. Could you please read that specific part as in your recollection it should read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, twice it's been repeated, something 1992, 1993. And what should this be in relation to, is that the translation should be that this was some time, the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993, that is, to be more precise, that this lasted some six months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. If you then would turn to page 8. You added two words in the right margin at approximately one-third of the page. It seems to contain 155 millimetre. Could you please read that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It seems to me that I had said "155 millimetres."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Rather than -- instead of 152 or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Maybe 155. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It can be checked. Then you added a few words a little bit below where it starts reading "Da li" could you please read those words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Where smoke and tracer shells produced and this was in relation to mortar shells, mostly." Here the translation is a little unclear, but that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for this clarification. Then on page 9 you added one word on the first line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was what my main duties were in the warehouse. And so I added, I think that's what I said more or less, that my main duty was first of all to organise the guard duty of the warehouse. And that on the orders of the logistics base I should issue means. And then from the production I should receive, means into the warehouse. And further on the text is more or less the same. It corresponds. There is a problem in relation to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have on -- you added I think one word in the right margin a little bit lower. It seems to part with a "P." I can't read it. Could you read what you added there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here I added, clarified, what cannot be heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You filled in the word where a question mark appears in the text; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What word would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That this was in the period while care was taken about saving ammunition, and to plan the use of ammunition precisely, according to the tasks given that was supposed to be carried out. That's, more or less, what should be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then I see some smaller correction mainly on the calibres as it seems, further down. You corrected numbers, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here there is in military terminology, one knows that when one says 762, that means 7.62 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it says 14 and a half. I only wrote 14.5. Then 42 -- 40 is repeated on two occasions, that's not necessary. And then for the Howitzer, I think, instead of 82 it should say 76. Perhaps that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we turn to the text page, page 10. Could you please read what you corrected in the first paragraph, that's also again, I think about calibres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's the same case here. It has to do with 18, it's not calibre 82. It says but 90, but it should say 76.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then a few lines further there seems to be a part inaudible. Could you please explain what you said there or what is in your recollection what the answer should have been at the very end where it reads "tenkovske mine i" at the end of this first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that. But I can't put anything else here in the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, if you can't, it is no problem. May I take it that almost at the end where you have stricken out some words, that they should be just stricken out because they make no sense or...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Words are repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they are not necessary here. The sense is lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And on then page 11, perhaps, first the first paragraph where you underlined a part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it says that during the first two years I wasn't included, I didn't participate in the maintenance. When I was in the logistics base, I was the commander of the warehouse. But on the grounds of my barracks a maintenance support company had been established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose of which was to maintain technical and material equipment. Furthermore, weapons were taken there to be repaired, vehicles were taken there to be serviced, repaired, and in the nearby factory, to the nearby factory, Famos Koran, which similarly had men and spare parts that could be used to repair vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that the rest of the page, these are mainly textual corrections? If there is anything that is of importance, would you say, "no, that needs further explanation or clarification," please indicate that clearly. We then turn to page 12 where you added one word approximately on one-third of the page. It seems to be something like "opravlijali." Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it has to do with artillery weapons. I said if the defects were fairly serious, in that case the weapon would be taken to the workshop. But if minor defects were in question, then people from the workplace, from the workshop would be sent to the locations where these weapons were located, and they would repair the weapons on site. That was a procedure which was well known in the army and a procedure that was followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is also approximately what we find in the English text, as far as my recollection goes. Mr. DP30, I take it that the other are rather textual issues. Then we turn to page 13. You underlined in the first paragraph a few words. Was that a clarification or could you explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the translation is not clear in that as units asked to be brought up to strength, well, I said that units would send their requests to their superior command, that is to say to lower units in their brigade, in the command of its brigade, and then the request would be relayed to the corps from there. And it would then be forwarded to the Main Staff for the sake of bringing up to strength.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that the other marks you made on page 13 are just textual corrections, and would that be true for page 14 as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The translation is fairly good, but the order should be somewhat changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what you indicated. Then we turn to page 15. You added two words just after you, for the first time, mentioned the name of General Kovacevic. Two words are added. Could you please read them. I think you filled in what was inaudible. Page 15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At the end of 1992. Here it says "incomprehensible" and you can just see the number two that has been noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever there is anything that needs further clarification, please indicate so. But I now turn to page 16. First paragraph, you added one word and you underlined.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the whole it concerns the fact that as time passed by, the technical equipment got -- the quality of the technical equipment deteriorated and it was worn out, it became worn out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the other parts of page 16, are these textual? I see that sometimes you just have stricken out words that appear again. Are these all textual rather than...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is a lot of repetition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if we turn to page 17. Would that be approximately the same or would you like to comment on any of the underlinings or marks you made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think the question was put exactly as it was in English. It hasn't been entirely reproduced. I think it said "during the inspections, examinations, what sort of problems did you notice in the brigade?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are now talking about the first line of page 17, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any of the other underlinings need specific attention on this page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, words are repeated, what I have underlined. Perhaps the order should just be changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it does not substantially affect the content of your answers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not substantially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn to page 18.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here I would like to clarify something. On page 17, paragraph 4. The reason for which weapons were not cleaned after that had been used, that's what I said. However, an additional clarification is required. It was wartime after all, so weapons had to be maintained in the field. Combat activity didn't make it possible for the weapons to be cleaned on a daily basis, and there are other reasons that one could mention, and I have already mentioned certain things in response to questions put to me by the Defence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. We then turn to page 18. It seems that you have stricken out in the middle of the page a relatively longer part of the text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In response to the question "How did the logistics base function within the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?" I said that the assistant for logistics, Colonel Krsmanovic, and his assistant was Milivoje Solar who unified the work of logistics services, the technical service, the quartermaster service, the medical service for a certain period of time there was a representative of the veterinary service, and the representative of the construction service there. So these were services that functioned in 1995 on the whole when I was within the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying this. Does any of the other corrections need specific attention on this page or is it rather textual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the clarification below where I have underlined something, it says "incomprehensible." So that I said that on the whole the other commands at various levels, the superior levels and the commands of the logistic base, I said that they had a similar structure to the logistics base, to logistics organ, and that the financial service entered that structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then may I ask you to turn to page 19, especially in the middle of the page you underlined a bit more. Would that need some explanation or -- I hope that you understand that I cannot see the original text, so I have to try to find out what needs specific attention and what not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just would like to say that this question concerned the period during which I was already in the corps, and it doesn't really refer to this -- to what is the subject of the discussion today, but in the translation certain words are repeated twice, even three times. It refers to the fact that we had, with Colonel Krsmanovic as assistant for the corps logistics, we had daily meetings with him in the morning at 8.00 when we dealt with issues concerning logistics security, and discussed unit's requests. We were then given priority tasks for that day and we forwarded their requests to the superior command in relation to the logistics security in services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if none of the other -- I don't know whether any of the other changes on page 19 needs further explanation or clarification, or is it just textual? I see that there are a lot of repetitious words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I mentioned an example. We weren't always at the logistics command post, but also at forward command post to help with the logistic security, to help with the organisation of logistic security when the Muslim side was preparing an attack on the whole, we were then sent to those forward commands as help for lower units and units which would come to help the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's also approximately how it reads in the English text. Could we then turn to page 20. And in page 20 I see three big question marks approximately in the middle and also that you are connecting one part of the text to another part. Could you please explain what is in the second half of the page, what your problem was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand why in the English text, and it has been translated like this here too, I don't know whether it is some kind of provocation or humiliation, but I explained that the corps command was located in Lukavica where I was on duty in the corps, and that the logistics command place was in Pale, and that if necessary they would form forward commands if or rather when defensive actions were planned or actions to take back positions that had been taken by the other side. But here it says, just trying to remember the right expression, but the previous response was given, but the response was given previously. That's not -- that can't be correct because it seems that I said that. It is "incomprehensible" that's what it says again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So proper attention should be paid to that. Could we then perhaps turn to page 21. I see that there are some corrections as far as the calibres are concerned, 7.65, 40.5. "Broving" is "Browning."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the last three lines I see that you have underlined a word "nerazumljivo," something like that. Could you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That has to do with the question that I discussed yesterday. I said that the 27th logistics base wasn't under direct command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, but I said that in accordance with the military rules, that was possible or rather that's how it was according to our rules in the JNA. The corps had its logistics base, that it relied on directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then next page, 22. Is there any need to explain? I see that you underlined the word "multiple" in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Again, the word "Romanija" is repeated above, and I underlined. It should say whether the reports came from the both sides and that they could be checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you underline the word "multiple" where it reads in the English: "Would receive multiple reports from the logistics base." Could you please explain why you underlined multiple?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I underlined it because it wasn't translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the rest of the page, is that textual or is that a fact of content?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think the translation is correct here, as far as reports are concerned. So reports were sent to the superior command, daily reports, depending on the issue, if it was the production of ammunition and taking it into the warehouse and then perhaps weekly reports or reports submitted every two weeks or every few months depending on what had been ordered by the superior command and what had been requested by the superior command. And that would also include semi-annual and annual reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please turn, if possible to page 23. I see that you underlined in the sixth paragraph three words, " sta ce trebalo" something like that. Could you explain that. Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question as it was put to me, well, it's not comprehensible. I can't explain that. I can't clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I think that the sense could be explained too. I didn't follow that in English because I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that the other corrections are rather of a textual character?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. Some words are unnecessarily repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could we please turn to page 24. Is that all textual rather than related to the content?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, especially towards the end. The penultimate paragraph, it has to do with the translation which is not correct. It should state that some of the requests from the units themselves weren't dealt with by us. Everything went through the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how we should read that part of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then turn to page 25. You especially underlined quite some words in the second paragraph. Could you explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, certain words were repeated. It is not necessary. It says the same twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so it is rather textual than content. Then in the middle of the page you made -- is that also a repetition of words or is that -- does that need some explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is probably a problem in the translation. The line of your deployment, that's not very comprehensible. It is not clear in this context, in the context of the question. Perhaps it is not like that in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the English has the -- the question has been put in English so we will finally be able to see what question has been put to you at that very moment and see whether the answer is comprehensible in that respect. Could we then turn to page 26. Is that a fact of content?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, there are certain repetitions. Perhaps twice it says that the Main Staff tasked or gave a deployment order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we would then turn to page 27, that seems to be all textual, rather than -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, mostly. There are some repetitions of some words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 28, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You, on the third paragraph where you -- a question is put to you, you underlined certain words there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the answer was different but I heard that he was the Chief of Staff of General Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we come to page 29.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where it says "incomprehensible" it should say, "until the command of the logistics base has been established, which that is -- was imprisoned until the 6th of June 1992 when the command got out of Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The other corrections you made, do they effect substantially the content or...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Substantially, it doesn't change the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that you've come to this page and then you were not able to finish the last two pages. The Chamber will consider whether you will be invited to do the last pages as well. But we first need a break. So we will continue after the break. We will adjourn until 10 minutes past 10.00 -- past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two counsel standing at the same time. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Before you render a decision regarding this document, so that we don't waste any more time, and so that we can allow the Prosecution the time to explain their position, I just would like to briefly state some things. But I think they are very important things to be said. May I have your leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- As brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I wish to say is the following: We are going to need some rapidity to read the documents at the same time, parallelly. We have come to page 20 and what we are going to see is that this witness -- this witness was seen certain things, has not seen other things and I am going to show this in the following way, Mr. President. If we look at page -- I will just take the most obvious things, if we look at page 10, for instance, at the end of the page we have something that seems to be -- have been interpreted as probably over 300.000 tons, et cetera. Now, if you look at page corresponding to the Serbian text, and I will give you the page straight away, and we only have 3.000 tons, not 300.000 tons. And if we continue on to the following page, there are mistakes of the same type, but in order not to waste time, I would like us to look at page 13 in Serbian, which should correspond to page 13 or 14 in the English version, and it corresponds -- yes. Could you please look at page 13 of the English text. Examine the most important paragraph on this page which begins with "as anywhere in the army" and to compare it with page 13 of the Serb transcript which begins with the first paragraph, the word "Kao," you will see, Mr. President, in the middle of the Serb text that in the middle of the Serb text, it says "towards the Main Staff" which has not at all been translated in the English text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... The inconsistencies and I think, as a matter of fact, and on page 13, the witness has clarified the issue. But it is not clear in my recollection whether it was page 13, but I think he did. The Chamber is fully aware of that and is certainly -- will not just accept these documents in the form as they are. That's -- but, Mr. Ierace asked for an indication. Is there anything else you would like to draw the attention of the Chamber to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Just simply in relation to the cross-examination of the Prosecution, we have to know what is going to be done with these documents, bearing in mind that there are things that have escaped the attention of the witness, specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace asked for an indication. Mr. Ierace, you were on your feet. Did you want to add something or were you just waiting for the indication you asked for?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just that, Mr. President, that pursuant to your request earlier this morning, I approached the Defence during the break to discuss the two issues, one being when we would receive the details for the witnesses in January, the dates of births and ranks. I noticed over the break we have now received a letter which contains the dates of births of two of these witnesses that the Defence seeks to add to the witness list. I am told by the Defence that they cannot tell us when we will get the additional information, just that we will get it as soon as possible. In relation to the appendixes to the reports, much the same. I asked the Defence whether there was any progress, any difference between what they have told me today and what they said three weeks ago, and effectively, they said no, no difference. So, Mr. President, the Prosecution is not in a position to agree to the four witnesses being added to the witness list for the Defence, in these circumstances, nor can we be ready in the first week in January to cross-examine those witnesses without having a proper period of time to make our inquiries. And in relation to the appendixes I would be grateful if the Trial Chamber would fix a date to which the Prosecution is to receive the appendixes in a language of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that these are not new witnesses, but just a change of witnesses. We do not want to add new witnesses, four new witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue is when does the Prosecution receive ranks and dates of birth, that's the issue. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I replied to Mr. Ierace earlier that we have done everything that was necessary, that is, we have done the impossible trying to contact the people who would be able to give us this information, and that if we managed to do this immediately after 2.00 p.m. this afternoon, we will communicate this to Mr. Ierace. I was very clear. I cannot guarantee things that I don't know about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, the Presiding Judges and the Chamber would like to be informed by 6.00 this evening if the Defence would not have managed to give the ranks and dates of birth of all these four witnesses to the Prosecution and we will further consider the translation of the annexes. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, just a very brief clarification. In our submission of the 6th of December, the Defence informed the Chamber and gave precisions as to its submission of the 29th of November this year, in a sense that we changed the order of -- calling order of witnesses. So in our submission of the 6th of December, we clarified that we were not adding new witnesses to the list, but that the four existing witnesses that are already on the list that has been submitted, we are changing that with four new witnesses. So it is in this sense we just were replacing them. So four new ones are being replaced by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who did raise the issue of this being new witnesses rather than replacing -- old witnesses replacing other ones? I think the issue at this very moment is ranks and dates of birth. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And without that information, we oppose the addition of these new witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. So the issue is -- and that's what I would like to be informed about by 6.00 this afternoon -- whether the Defence has been able to give ranks and dates of birth to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Ierace, you asked for an indication -- yes. The Chamber gives the following indication to you, that if we would have to consider the admission into evidence of the previous statements, a statement given by Witness DP30, that the Chamber will consider to admit it into evidence if it receives, first, the audio tape of the interview, then it would receive the transcripts, both in English and B/C/S, as we have seen them today, with all the markings made by the witness so that we can better understand the transcript of today's session where the witness explains about these markings. We would then need a transcript of the original words spoken, whether it is in B/C/S or in English, so that would be a mixed transcript, reflecting what the investigators have said in English and what the response has been by Mr. DP30 in B/C/S. So that would be a mixed transcript, and not as it is now, either English. So we would have the original words spoken in that transcript, and we would then like to have an official translation of that mixed transcript into English, so that there is a full possibility to reconstruct precisely what has been said, and that we are not dependent on translations that were made on the spot which might not be complete or what might still contain errors. Because we have seen that there are some differences in the translation as it was done by the translators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: therefore, the translation work done at that time might have been to the best of the abilities of the interpreters but is not a sufficient basis to accept the documents as they are. Then you may proceed -- after I have given this indication, you know what the Prosecution would have to provide in order to have these statements considered to be accepted, to be admitted into evidence. Yes, Madam Usher, could you please escort Witness DP30 into the courtroom. Could you, Mr. Ierace, could you consider whether you would need the last few pages, whether we have to ask the witness to go through the -- I don't know what the relevance is, otherwise we could perhaps limit it to those parts. But of course the Defence is in a position to say, well, these pages are very relevant for us. If you could do without these last two pages, we would not have to ask the witness to work even harder than we all do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. DP30. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing, Mr. President. The Defence is very concerned about the time. The Prosecution wanted to produce this in order to save time, and it is already now half past 11.00, so if we can speed things up, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you have heard, Witness, we have some time problems. If you can answer properly in a few words my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the usher can assist us by moving the ELMO slightly so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have a line of sight to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir you mentioned amongst the weapons at antitank guided rockets, 9K to 11. Were they in your warehouse, those -- that particular weapon, type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rockets 9K-11 and they were in my warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does "9K-11" refer to? Is that simply the model number of that system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a Russian guided rocket, it is an antitank rocket, 9K-11 is its marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And how is the rocket guided? Is it by a wire or some other system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rocket is guided by a wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So does that mean that the operator controls the path of the rocket by means of a wire, that is, communications along a wire between his control mechanism and the rocket during its flight so that it can be steered onto the target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know in that set there is also a control board to control -- to guide the rocket and it can -- the rocket can be guided up to the target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Were there any of those weapons in your warehouse in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my warehouse there were, as I already said, all types of ammunition and ordnance equipment, mines and explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Including that particular system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I recall. These were smaller reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know what the range was of that rocket system? In other words how far could that rocket travel from where it was launched in that guided fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know because that's not my field of expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it also in stock in 1993 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall while I was at the warehouse, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever deliver any of those systems to any of the brigades of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in 1992, 1993, or 1994 up until August of that year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of deliveries issuing not only to the SRK and also to the Drina Corps, and there was also distribution among the logistics base, on the basis of the order of the Main Staff. So I really wouldn't be able to tell you exactly whether this particular delivery took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But had the brigades wanted them, they were available in that period of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had asked for them, the Main Staff would have probably approved that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday you were asked some questions about the nature of tracer bullets and incendiary rounds. Do you know what it is in a tracer bullet which allows it to be seen in flight? What chemical substance is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a chemical substance which ignites and you can see the trace, the latter -- the end part of the bullet, of the bullet of the round which is flying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Depending on the length of flight of the bullet, does that substance continue to burn and thus produce light after it hits its target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it is burning throughout the flight of the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Tell us, what is the difference, therefore, between a tracer round and an incendiary round?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is in the tracer round you can see its flight; and in an incendiary round when it hits an obstacle, an explosion takes place and the incendiary substance is lit up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Therefore, can we assume that if the round does not explode when it hits its target, but instead ricochets, more or less intact, and if it is producing light then it is a tracer round, not an incendiary round?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question well. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's okay. I withdraw that question. I will move on to a different topic. In reviewing the transcript yesterday afternoon, did you notice that at one point you were asked what weapons, that is, what infantry weapons you held in your warehouse. Do you remember reading that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mentioned, amongst other weapons, pistols, semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could this be done in the presence of the witness or do we have to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, I think we can, because we are now speaking about something which is probably not what is going to be accepted by your Chamber later or at another time, because you asked the Prosecution to do something else earlier. Therefore, we are now speaking about the text which is not going to be in the existence in its form, and it could cause technical problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I take it that you were referring to page 21 of the -- yes. We just went through the transcript and it is my clear recollection that we specifically paid attention to that part so that there should be no problem. The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you still have in front of you the B/C/S, that is, the transcript in Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian, Witness? I think you are looking at it now; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please turn to page 21 and I think halfway down that page you indicate a number of infantry weapons that were kept in your storehouse for distribution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for distribution, those were weapons which were within the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they -- did they come from your warehouse before they went to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. How do you know that the weaponry in that paragraph was in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, let's say, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that I was the chief of the technical service in the corps in 1995, and that I know what kind of weapons there were in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please read from the top of that page alongside the initials "RP"

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am told that there is an error in the transcript. I didn't hear it because I was doing something else. But the witness apparently mentioned a different date than the one -- a date different from the one that we can see in the transcript. In the transcript it is "1993." We could ask the question again. And I would like to take this opportunity to ask how much time remains for the Prosecution, because all this work which has been done and which concerns the transcript should be time taken from the Prosecution's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand your position. I am not indicating at this very moment how much time will still be left for the Prosecution. We will consider that. Where -- could you tell me where I find "1993" in the transcript and what line --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 43, line 8, Mr. President. [In English] "Let's say in 1993." [Interpretation] 1993 apparently is not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it is a question. It is a question, so no one considers this to be what the witness said. I think it is the question. Mr. Ierace, could you please check. It is my recollection that's what you asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. President. The witness indicated that he understood at that time he was listing the weaponry, which was in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, could you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then of course in his answer he mentioned 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please read from the top of the page alongside the first reference to the initials "RP" and please read it slowly so that we can hear the translation as you read it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says: "I will return to a question which I have already asked, it is a fairly technical question" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP30, could you please read slowly. If one reads, one usually speeds up. So would you please read slowly so the interpreters can follow what you say. Could you please restart.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I will go back to a question that I have already asked. It is a fairly technical question which concerns ammunition which was delivered from the 27th logistics base. I am particularly interested in weapons of a smaller calibre, that is to say, I am interested in hand weapons and ammunition. I know that there were many such weapons in the corps. "Could you tell me anything about these weapons, about such weapons?"

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please keep reading.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Well, yes, I could. It is not a secret. The pistols that there were were Russian TT-7.62 and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right stop there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Local pistols of homemade production of 7.62 millimetres --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we perhaps don't have the same text, but I didn't hear the witness read at the end the word "the kinds of rifles and" I didn't hear the witness say that. I don't know whether he has the same text or not. It is at the end of the paragraph concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate what words in B/C/S have not been read out by the witness? Because he was reading the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I think the last three words which I have just said "[B/C/S spoken]" the kinds of rifles and these last three words weren't read, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least I can follow you pronounced these words. Witness, is it true that you did not read the last three words, "[B/C/S spoken]"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't read them because I think that the question was about all the ammunition and I don't think the translation is good. I don't know what it says in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least you've now pronounced these words. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in reading that question that was asked of you, you said: "It is a fairly technical question which concerns ammunition which was delivered from the 27th logistics base. I am particularly interested in weapons of a smaller calibre, that is to say, I am interested in hand weapons and ammunition. I know that there were many such weapons in the corps. Can you tell me anything about these weapons, about such weapons?" Do you say that you understood that question to refer not to what you provided from your warehouse, but rather what the corps had; is that what you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I understood that the weapons delivered to the corps, according to my understanding, those are the kinds of weapons the corps had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you agree that before you were asked that question at that point of the interview you were asked earlier what type of infantry weapons you had in your storehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember such a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And did you have in your storehouse Russian pistols, TT-7.62?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had them for my military unit, in accordance with the military establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, yes or no, did you have that weapon in your storehouse at any stage between 1992 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have an objection that concerns the relevance, Mr. President, because I don't see what relevance the pistol could have in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question has been answered, so there is no use to decide on the objection any more. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have machine-guns in your storehouse, warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only had them for my unit, my military unit. So that was the technical warehouse, technical ammunition warehouse of the 27th logistics base.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, in your storehouse did you have ammunition for infantry weapons for distribution to forces of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any rifles for distribution to forces of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only as part of the reserves. I had 7.9 millimetre rifles which were taken either from Visoko or Hadzici. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were they M-76s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you saying that the only rifles that you had in your warehouse between 1992 and 1994 for distribution to forces of the VRS were 7.9 millimetre rifles taken from either Visoko or Hadzici; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP30 [Resumed]
